technical_principles.principle: Style rules decide which skills are worth training time.
technical_principles.details: Folkstyle rewards sustained control, riding, mat returns, escapes, reversals, and near-fall work. Freestyle rewards takedowns, exposure, turns, step-outs, and fast par terre conversion. Greco-Roman removes lower-body attacks and shifts training toward pummeling, upper-body control, throws, lifts, and par terre.

technical_principles.principle: Control and exposure are different scoring languages.
technical_principles.details: Folkstyle requires control to score takedowns, reversals, riding time, and near-fall situations. Freestyle and Greco can score from exposure, danger positions, throws, step-outs, and par terre actions without the same long riding incentive.

technical_principles.principle: The first score is not the end of the exchange.
technical_principles.details: Folkstyle takedowns must connect to ride, turn, or safe release strategy. Freestyle takedowns must connect immediately to lace, gut wrench, lift, or edge-aware reset prevention. Greco upper-body scores must connect to par terre lock acquisition before the referee restarts.

technical_principles.principle: Bottom wrestling is central in folkstyle and narrower in international styles.
technical_principles.details: Folkstyle athletes need stand-ups, sit-outs, switches, granby options, hand control, hip heists, mat-return defense, and reversal awareness. Freestyle and Greco bottom/par terre defense prioritizes belly-down safety, hip pressure, lock breaking, exposure denial, and short-window survival.

technical_principles.principle: The boundary is tactical, not a pause button.
technical_principles.details: Freestyle and Greco include step-out scoring and continuation principles. Folkstyle increasingly keeps action live with minimal inbounds contact, so athletes need edge finishes, safe mat returns, and avoidance of fleeing/stalling behavior.

technical_principles.principle: Stalling and passivity rules punish non-improvement.
technical_principles.details: Folkstyle stalling targets backing out, clinging, failure to improve, and top/bottom inactivity. Freestyle activity time and Greco passivity/ordered par terre change strategy, making purposeful ties, attacks, turn attempts, and center control trainable match skills.

technical_principles.principle: Technique libraries must be filtered by rule set and level.
technical_principles.details: Greco profiles must block leg attacks, trips, and below-waist holds. All styles require neck, spine, shoulder, knee, slam, full-nelson, scissor, and dangerous-position safeguards. Youth and beginner progressions should delay high-amplitude throws, complex rolls, and uncontrolled lifts.

technical_principles.principle: Competition week shifts from capacity building to freshness, weigh-in compliance, and tactical sharpness.
technical_principles.details: Training volume should taper while maintaining stance, hand-fight feel, first attacks, short par terre/top-bottom sequences, and recovery. Weight management must avoid dehydration-driven practices and use certified minimum weights, hydration, nutrition, and skin checks.

beginner.priority: Build safe stance, motion, falling, hand position, basic attack/defense shapes, and simple rule awareness before complex live exchanges.
beginner.folkstyle_focus: Neutral stance and motion, penetration step, sprawl, go-behind, tight waist, wrist control, safe base, stand-up, hip heist, and belly-down pin defense.
beginner.freestyle_focus: Same neutral base plus step-out awareness, safe exposure concepts, immediate belly-down defense, and simple gut-wrench/turn defense before advanced laces or throws.
beginner.greco_focus: Pummeling posture, inside control, underhook/overhook safety, arm drag, snap, body-position awareness, and no below-waist contact habits.

intermediate.priority: Connect positions into chains and train rule-specific scoring decisions under guided resistance.
intermediate.folkstyle_focus: Shot setup to finish to ride, mat returns, breakdown to turn, escape/reversal chains, riding-time awareness, edge finishes, and stalling avoidance.
intermediate.freestyle_focus: Feet-to-back attacks, reattacks, step-out pressure, takedown-to-turn transitions, gut wrench, leg lace, par terre defense, and activity-time urgency.
intermediate.greco_focus: Pummel-to-attack systems, arm throws, body locks, duck/drag variations without leg contact, lift entries, gut wrench, par terre defense, and passivity strategy.
intermediate.session_design: Use short-goes from exact rule states: 20-second ride, 30-second activity, edge finish, par terre turn window, bottom escape, and late-score protection.

advanced.priority: Specialize by body type, rule set, opponent tendencies, score-clock state, and competition format.
advanced.folkstyle_focus: Opponent-specific ride/escape plans, return chains, near-fall series, riding-time math, overtime strategy, referee/stalling management, and tactical optional starts/releases.
advanced.freestyle_focus: High-value action selection, exposure-risk management, challenge-aware scoring clarity, par terre lock races, edge traps, shot-clock tactics, and score-criteria awareness.
advanced.greco_focus: Tie dominance, passivity creation, ordered par terre scoring, lift mechanics, high-amplitude threat, no-leg scramble discipline, and tie-break criteria awareness.
advanced.competition_week: Reduce live volume, keep intensity through brief scoring bursts, rehearse first-period tactics, protect weight/hydration, and prioritize skin checks, sleep, and recovery.

drills_or_practice_design.name: Style Split Rules Walkthrough
drills_or_practice_design.design: Teach one exchange three ways: folkstyle takedown-to-ride, freestyle takedown-to-lace or gut, Greco pummel-to-body-lock-to-par-terre. Stop after each scoring event and ask athletes what the referee awards and what the next best action is.

drills_or_practice_design.name: Folkstyle Escape-Reversal Chain
drills_or_practice_design.design: Start bottom in referee position. Bottom must win hand control, build base, stand or sit-out, then choose escape or reversal. Top scores by mat return, ride extension, or turn. Use 20- to 40-second goes.

drills_or_practice_design.name: Freestyle Takedown-to-Turn Window
drills_or_practice_design.design: Neutral attack begins at moderate resistance. After takedown, offensive athlete has a short clock to lock gut wrench or leg lace; defender wins by belly-down pressure, hip block, and lock denial.

drills_or_practice_design.name: Greco Pummel-to-Ordered-Par-Terre
drills_or_practice_design.design: Begin from over-under or two-on-one pummeling. Athletes score by creating clear upper-body attack or passivity pressure. Then restart in par terre and train lock acquisition, lift/gut attempt, and bottom exposure denial.

drills_or_practice_design.name: Edge Scoring Constraints
drills_or_practice_design.design: Start with one foot or knee near the boundary. Offensive athlete finishes inbounds or scores step-out when legal; defender circles, squares, or counters without fleeing. Emphasize continuation and safe landing space.

drills_or_practice_design.name: Activity and Stalling Short-Go
drills_or_practice_design.design: Use referee commands and a visible clock. Athletes must create a real attack, improvement, turn attempt, escape, or center-control action before the clock expires. Score penalties or activity points according to the selected style.

drills_or_practice_design.name: Near-Fall and Exposure Defense
drills_or_practice_design.design: Start in controlled danger positions. Folkstyle defender fights out of near-fall criteria while top maintains legal pinning pressure. International-style defender denies exposure counts and rolls through only when technically safe.

drills_or_practice_design.name: Competition Week Microcycle
drills_or_practice_design.design: Early week: brief high-quality live and position-specific goes. Midweek: tactical first attacks, edge, top/bottom or par terre. Day before: weight-compliant movement, hand-fight feel, short starts, skin check, hydration, sleep, and recovery.

common_errors.error: Training one universal wrestling game instead of style-specific scoring.
common_errors.correction: Tag every drill with style, scoring target, legal actions, restart condition, and winning behavior.

common_errors.error: Folkstyle athletes can attack from neutral but cannot escape, reverse, or avoid rides.
common_errors.correction: Program bottom skills every week: hand control, base, stand-up, sit-out, switch, mat-return defense, and ride clock awareness.

common_errors.error: Freestyle athletes finish takedowns and pause instead of attacking par terre immediately.
common_errors.correction: Attach a turn window to takedown drills and assess lock speed, hip position, and defender belly-down response.

common_errors.error: Greco athletes reach, block, trip, or counter with the legs from habits learned in folkstyle/freestyle.
common_errors.correction: Use Greco-only constraints during pummeling and defense: hips, chest, arms, head position, and footwork without below-waist contact.

common_errors.error: Athletes treat the boundary as a restart instead of a scoring zone.
common_errors.correction: Run edge-specific short-goes and penalize fleeing, backing straight out, or stopping before the whistle.

common_errors.error: Athletes wait for referee calls instead of creating visible activity.
common_errors.correction: Train attack frequency, tie improvement, center pressure, turn attempts, and referee-command response under clock constraints.

common_errors.error: Beginners are exposed to high-amplitude throws, hard mat returns, or complex rolls before they can fall, brace, and protect joints.
common_errors.correction: Require breakfall, neck-safe posture, controlled partner lift, and technical landing gates before live high-risk actions.

common_errors.error: Competition preparation relies on dehydration or rapid weight loss instead of skill sharpness and certified weight planning.
common_errors.correction: Use certified minimum weight, gradual descent, hydration monitoring, nutrition planning, and reduced late-week training load.

safety_constraints.constraint: Do not prescribe dehydration, fasting, sauna/sweat-suit cutting, diuretics, or other rapid weight-loss practices.
safety_constraints.backend_action: Flag unsafe weight-loss language and route to certified medical, dietitian, or governing-body weight-management guidance.

safety_constraints.constraint: Suspicious, draining, or contagious skin conditions require removal from contact and qualified medical clearance according to competition rules.
safety_constraints.backend_action: Add hygiene prompts for daily skin checks, clean gear, showering, and mat disinfection in wrestling plans.

safety_constraints.constraint: High-amplitude throws, lifts, and hard mat returns require supervised progression, landing skill, partner control, and adequate mat space.
safety_constraints.backend_action: Block advanced throw/lift drills for beginner profiles unless prerequisites are met.

safety_constraints.constraint: Avoid actions that force the head, neck, or spine into dangerous flexion, twisting, or uncontrolled impact.
safety_constraints.backend_action: Include stop conditions for neck pain, head impact, numbness, loss of control, or illegal pressure.

safety_constraints.constraint: Illegal holds and potentially dangerous positions involving full nelsons, scissoring, twisting knees, forced shoulders, or uncontrolled submissions must be excluded from training plans.
safety_constraints.backend_action: Filter technique recommendations against rule-set legal-action lists and athlete level.

safety_constraints.constraint: Stop or regress live wrestling when fatigue causes head-down shooting, uncontrolled throws, poor landing, or inability to defend safely.
safety_constraints.backend_action: Use shorter goes, more rest, or lower resistance when technical safety markers fail.

sport_training_rules.rule: Every wrestling drill must declare style_scope before technique selection.
sport_training_rules.then: tag drill as folkstyle, freestyle, greco_roman, or multi_style and apply legal-action filters
sport_training_rules.rationale: Rule sets reward different outcomes and prohibit different actions.

sport_training_rules.rule: Greco-Roman profiles must exclude attacks below the waist.
sport_training_rules.then: block leg attacks, trips, leg laces, ankle picks, singles, doubles, high crotches, and leg-based counters
sport_training_rules.rationale: Greco-Roman forbids grasping below the belt line, tripping, and active leg use against the opponent.

sport_training_rules.rule: Folkstyle plans require recurring bottom wrestling.
sport_training_rules.then: include escape, reversal, base, hand control, mat-return defense, and ride-defense content weekly
sport_training_rules.rationale: Escape/reversal scoring and riding-time/control incentives make bottom wrestling a core skill domain.

sport_training_rules.rule: Freestyle takedown training should include immediate par terre conversion.
sport_training_rules.then: append short turn window for gut wrench, leg lace, exposure attack, or lock denial defense
sport_training_rules.rationale: Freestyle rewards rapid exposure and repeated turns after the initial score.

sport_training_rules.rule: Greco sessions should prioritize upper-body tie dominance and par terre.
sport_training_rules.then: bias content toward pummeling, underhook/overhook, two-on-one, body lock, arm throw, lift mechanics, gut wrench, and par terre defense
sport_training_rules.rationale: Without leg attacks, upper-body control and passivity/par terre phases dominate scoring opportunities.

sport_training_rules.rule: Edge wrestling must be practiced as a scoring and safety skill.
sport_training_rules.then: include boundary starts, step-out awareness, continuation, safe mat returns, and fleeing/stalling avoidance
sport_training_rules.rationale: Modern rule sets keep edge action meaningful through step-outs, continuation, and stricter inbounds definitions.

sport_training_rules.rule: Activity and stalling behavior must be trained under time constraints.
sport_training_rules.if: session includes live or situational wrestling
sport_training_rules.then: use short clocks requiring attack, improvement, turn attempt, escape, or center-control action
sport_training_rules.rationale: Passivity, activity time, and stalling calls directly affect match outcomes.

sport_training_rules.rule: Scoring drills should require the next rule-specific action.
sport_training_rules.then: continue to ride/turn/escape/par_terre/edge_reset according to style instead of stopping immediately
sport_training_rules.rationale: Match-winning wrestling depends on transitions after scores.

sport_training_rules.rule: Beginners must clear safety prerequisites before live complex positions.
sport_training_rules.then: prioritize stance, motion, breakfall, sprawl, base, hand safety, posture, and controlled partner contact
sport_training_rules.rationale: Complex scrambles, lifts, and rolls increase neck, knee, shoulder, and landing risk without foundations.

sport_training_rules.rule: Advanced training should include score-clock-criteria scenarios.
sport_training_rules.then: add late-match lead protection, deficit scoring, tie criteria, riding-time math, activity/passivity strategy, and challenge-aware clarity
sport_training_rules.rationale: Rule literacy changes optimal decisions near the end of periods and matches.

planning_rules.rule: During competition week, reduce volume before reducing technical sharpness.
planning_rules.then: favor short high-quality stance, hand-fight, first-attack, top/bottom or par terre, edge, and recovery work
planning_rules.rationale: Freshness, weight compliance, and tactical clarity are higher priorities than new capacity.

planning_rules.rule: Weight planning must not use dehydration-based methods.
planning_rules.then: use certified minimum weight, gradual descent, hydration, meals, sleep, and medical/dietitian referral when needed
planning_rules.rationale: Official wrestling programs and sports medicine sources discourage rapid dehydration and unsafe weight cutting.

planning_rules.rule: Competition plans should include skin and hygiene checks.
planning_rules.then: prompt clean gear, showering, mat cleaning, skin inspection, and medical clearance for suspicious lesions
planning_rules.rationale: Skin infections are a known wrestling risk and can affect eligibility and team health.

planning_rules.rule: Tournament planning must account for repeated short high-intensity bouts.
planning_rules.then: limit extra live volume, plan warm-up repeatability, refueling, hydration, cooldown, and between-match tactical review
planning_rules.rationale: Wrestlers may compete multiple times in a day with weigh-in, recovery, and injury-risk constraints.

planning_rules.rule: Dual-meet and tournament weeks require different loading.
planning_rules.then: use sharper single-opponent tactical prep; if tournament, prepare multiple style/body-type scenarios and recovery between bouts
planning_rules.rationale: A dual often has one known opponent; tournaments require broader tactical and recovery readiness.

planning_rules.rule: Phase allocation should match the athlete's primary rule set.
planning_rules.then: folkstyle emphasizes neutral plus top/bottom; freestyle emphasizes neutral-to-par-terre and exposure; Greco emphasizes pummel/upper-body plus par terre
planning_rules.rationale: Training ratios should mirror scoring incentives and common match phases.

teaching_progressions.notes: For Greco, replace penetration leg attacks with pummel, arm drag, snap, duck, and body-position entries.
Assess both escape to neutral and reversal to control.
Top athlete must improve without illegal pressure or passive clinging.
Pair every attack progression with exposure defense and safe roll mechanics.
Maintain no below-waist contact constraints throughout the progression.
Use style-specific scoring and restart rules.

skill_assessments.assessment: Athlete can identify legal actions, scoring value, restart, and next best action for the selected style.
skill_assessments.pass_signal: Correctly explains at least 8 of 10 common situations for their style without cross-style errors.

skill_assessments.assessment: Folkstyle bottom athlete can escape or reverse under controlled resistance.
skill_assessments.pass_signal: Wins hand control, builds base, avoids near-fall, and earns escape or reversal in repeated 30-second starts.

skill_assessments.assessment: Folkstyle top athlete can ride, return, and create legal near-fall threat.
skill_assessments.pass_signal: Maintains control, returns stand-ups safely, improves position, and creates turn attempts without stalling or illegal pressure.

skill_assessments.assessment: Freestyle athlete converts takedown to par terre scoring threat.
skill_assessments.pass_signal: Attacks gut wrench, lace, or exposure within the assigned short window while keeping hips and lock position.

skill_assessments.assessment: Greco athlete attacks and defends without lower-body violations.
skill_assessments.pass_signal: Completes live pummel-to-attack and defense rounds with no below-waist grabs, trips, or leg blocks.

skill_assessments.assessment: Athlete uses the edge to score or recover without fleeing.
skill_assessments.pass_signal: Finishes, circles, counters, or step-out pressures appropriately in boundary starts under referee commands.

skill_assessments.assessment: Athlete demonstrates safe contact prerequisites for higher-risk drills.
skill_assessments.pass_signal: Shows breakfall, neck-safe posture, controlled mat return mechanics, partner awareness, and stop-command compliance.
